publicationStmt.publisher: Association of Computers and the Humanities

availability.ab: Freely available under a Creative Commons license.

catDesc.name: access terms and systems
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with access-related publication practices and attempts to reduce payment-based barriers to literature. Includes both issues of licensing and equity.

catDesc.name: annotation systems
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of manual and machine-assisted annotation as well as their related systems and interfaces. Also covers analysis of texts via annotation.

catDesc.name: anthropology
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the study of human behaviors, cultures, and the observation of these behaviors and cultures. Also includes reports on the pedagogical intersections of digital humanities and these academic subjects in the classroom setting.

catDesc.name: augmented and virtual reality
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with augmented forms of reality, which may include immersive technologies, virtual reality, and digital reconstructions.

catDesc.name: archaeology
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with archaeological findings, the practice of the discipline, or the history of ancient civilizations and cultural practices.

catDesc.name: archives
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with physical and digital archives and their maintenance. This also contains discussions on the study of archives and archival management systems.

catDesc.name: area studies
catDesc.term: geographical/cultural area studies: [fill in as needed]
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with any sort of particular geographic or cultural focus.

catDesc.name: citation analysis
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with citation practices and new or traditional forms of their analysis.

catDesc.name: classics
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with classics as a discipline, as well as its study in digital form.

catDesc.name: code studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the cultural and interpretive significance of code.

catDesc.name: collaboration
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with collaborative academic scholarship and publications. For crowd-sourced efforts see #translation instead.

catDesc.name: comics
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the creation and criticism of comics and graphic-intensive print publications like graphic novels. Also, comics and graphic novels in digital form.

catDesc.name: communication studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering methods of communication such as speeches, public relations, and marketing intiatives, but also the theoretical and statistical study of communication at the macro level. For finer detail analysis of specific texts and publications, see #content_analysis.

catDesc.name: qualitative analysis
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with qualitative analysis of the content of documents (texts, audio, images, or video).

catDesc.name: corpus-based analysis
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the creation and study of corpora, sometimes via linguistic analyses.

catDesc.name: computer science
catDesc.gloss: Articles directly concerned with issues of computer science or computer programming, as well as their implementation and practice by digital humanists.

catDesc.name: cultural criticism
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the discipline of cultural studies, the act of cultural criticism, and issues of representation and marginalization in the digital humanities. This also includes articles related to the decentralized network of scholars known as "#TransformDH".

catDesc.name: cultural heritage institutions
catDesc.gloss: Articles either concerned with the discovery and preservation of cultural, ethnic, or academic heritage, and the institutions in which preservation often occurs (museums, galleries, archives, libraries, etc.) See #glam for articles which address the digital humanities in these spaces.

catDesc.name: data analytics
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the analysis of raw data (whether textual or another form). Also includes all forms of data mining.

catDesc.name: data curation
catDesc.gloss: Articles about the curation and preservation of data. This includes issues of sustainable practices as well as physical and digital concerns about preservation strategies.

catDesc.name: data modeling
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the modeling of data (including text as data). This includes articles interested in the creation, design, and philosophical implications of modeling, simulations, and knowledge representation generally.

catDesc.name: data visualization
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the visual representation of data, techniques of data visualization, and effects of visualizations in comparison with other forms of knowledge representation.

catDesc.name: databases
catDesc.gloss: Articles conerned with databases, their design, use, effects, and preservation. See #infrastructure for more on data maintenance.

catDesc.name: digital humanities
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of digital humanities as a field or collection of practices: specifically, the landscape, history, and future of digital humanities.

catDesc.name: digitality
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of digitality and the unique nature of the digital medium, for both born-digital and digitized materials.

catDesc.name: digital libraries
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering digital libraries: digital or digitized library collections, and libraries of materials available digitally.

catDesc.name: digital literacy
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of information literacy, digital literacy, skills, and competencies.

catDesc.name: digitization
catDesc.gloss: Articles about digitization and its relevant data. Includes the conversion of non-digital materials to a digital format, or from one digital format to another. Also covers the tools and methods of digitization as well as related practices such as data cleaning, and critical perspectives on the effects of digitization.

catDesc.name: editing
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering theories, practices, and technologies of editing, especially as a scholarly practice.

catDesc.name: electronic literature
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of electronic literature, interactive fiction, chatbots, and related genres of creative digitally or algorithmically generated texts. Connected to #hypertext via hypertext fiction.

catDesc.name: ecocriticism
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of the environment, ecocriticism, and digital humanities through an environmental lens. This includes ecologically-focused projects which use digital humanities methods, environmental perspectives on digital humanities, and the environmental impact of digital materials.

catDesc.name: ethics
catDesc.gloss: Articles about ethics and best practices in the digital humanities, as well as in computing more generally.

catDesc.name: game studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles about games, game studies, and ludology. Includes video games, text adventures, and the study of organized play more generally.

catDesc.name: gender and sexuality studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of gender, sexuality, and related fields of study including gender and sexuality studies, trans studies, queer theory, and feminist approaches.

catDesc.name: geospatial analysis
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering mapping, digital humanities oriented towards physical and geographical space, geography as a field, and geospatial analysis methods and tools.

catDesc.name: GLAMs
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of digital humanities in GLAMs (Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums) and digital humanities done by cultural workers in GLAMs within and outside the academy.

catDesc.name: global digital humanities
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of global DH or digital humanities as an international community. Also, DH done via international collaborations with specific attention to an international audience, as well as issues of Eurocentrism in digital humanities.

catDesc.name: graphic design
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of the visual aspects of interface design and digital materials, or graphic design more broadly. Includes typography and font studies.

catDesc.name: history
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerning historical events or scholarly production methods, and historical materials.

catDesc.name: hypertext
catDesc.gloss: Articles about hypertext and hypertext technologies. Sometimes connected to #elit via hypertext fiction.

catDesc.name: image analysis
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of image studies and the processing or analysis of images as separate from the study of visual art. Often includes studies of photographic corpora.

catDesc.name: indigeneity
catDesc.gloss: Articles comprising indigenous and Native American studies, indigeneous communities and cultural materials, and indigeneity broadly speaking.

catDesc.name: information architecture
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with information architecture and system design. Specifically, the organization and design of information systems as separate from infrastructure.

catDesc.name: information science
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of informatics and information science. In this context, informatics may refer to the study of computational systems(related to computer science), or to the study of information preservation, collection or analysis (connected to information science, and sometimes connected to library science).

catDesc.name: information retrieval
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of information retrieval and discovery. This includes search engines, query languages, and browsing.

catDesc.name: infrastructure
catDesc.term: institutional support for digital projects and programs
catDesc.gloss: Articles about infrastructure for digital materials and the digital humanities. This can refer to physical infrastructure (e.g. servers and physical collections of digital materials), cyberinfrastructure, and organizational infrastructure that sustains DH initiatives.

catDesc.name: interdisciplinarity
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of interdisciplinary practice, the adaptation of practices from one discipline to another, disciplinarity in the academy, and interdisciplinary teams.

catDesc.name: studies of specific languages
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the study of specific languages (e.g. Nauhatl, Latin, etc., used with an IANA language code) or texts in those languages.

catDesc.name: linguistics
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of linguistics as a field and liguistic techniques in the digital humanities.

catDesc.name: literary studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the study of literature and poetry; digital approaches to literature and literary texts.

catDesc.name: machine learning
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with machine learning and artificial intelligence as well as their uses in the digital humanities.

catDesc.name: manuscripts
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering manuscripts and the study of manuscripts. This comprises transcription and preservation of manuscripts, digital collections of manuscripts, and digital tools for manuscript studies.

catDesc.name: markup languages
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of text encoding and markup languages. This includes XML, TEI, text editors, and studies of markup broadly speaking.

catDesc.name: materialisms
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of materialisms or the material turn in the humanities. Also covers the physical components of digital production (including hardware and physical demands on equipments and humans), and materialities in the digital humanities.

catDesc.name: media history
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the history of media, information systems, print technology, and computation.

catDesc.name: media studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of media, multimedia, and (new) media studies.

catDesc.name: medieval studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the Middle Ages, medieval materials (especially medieval texts), and medieval studies.

catDesc.name: metadata
catDesc.gloss: Articles about metadata and the study of metadata, metadata creation, as well as metadata standards.

catDesc.name: minimal computing
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of minimal computing as a field. Includes constraints in digital production and the digital humanities, as well as the use of minimal computing principles in digital projects.

catDesc.name: mobile applications
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of mobile technology. These may include: mobile applications, mobile design, adapting existing digital resources for mobile use, the unique nature of the mobile digital medium, or the use of mobile technologies.

catDesc.name: audiovisual media
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with moving images, including film, cinema, and other forms of audiovisual media. Also covers film and cinema studies as well as video technologies and their respective platforms.

catDesc.name: music
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering music, music history, and musicology as separate from sound and sound studies.

catDesc.name: networks
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of networks and network science. This includes social networks and peer networks as well as physical or data networks. See #social_media for that particular subset of networked interactions.

catDesc.name: natural language processing
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of NLP (natural language processing), sentiment analysis, language parsing, and other generative or interpretive interactions of computers with natural language.

catDesc.name: oral history
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the creation and study of oral histories, as well as methods for their preservation. Many articles under this term are published in an interview format.

catDesc.name: pedagogy
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of teaching, pedagogy, and the digital in the classroom.

catDesc.name: performing arts
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of performance, the performing arts, and performance studies. Includes performing art as a genre of fine art, dance, theatre, and spoken poetry.

catDesc.name: philosophy
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of philosophy and its application in the digital humanities, the appliation of digital humanities methods to philosophical study, and philosphies of digital humanities.

catDesc.name: project management
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of project mangement, project design, and workflows.

catDesc.name: project reports
catDesc.gloss: Articles comprising case studies, project reports, conference reports/reviews, and accounts of classes taught. Projects might include: events, websites, and other self-contained digital humanities efforts/outputs.

catDesc.name: public humanities
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of public history and public humanities (historical or humanistic work that faces or takes place outside the academic realm). Includes articles which do public history and humanities as well as articles about these fields.

catDesc.name: publishing
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering issues of publishing, especially in relation to the digital medium. Closely connected to #editing.

catDesc.name: race studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of race and race studies. This includes critical race studies, ethnic studies, and Africana studies.

catDesc.name: reading methods
catDesc.term: practices and technologies of reading and writing
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of reading. This comprises technologies and methods of reading, how the digital medium affects reading practices, and close/distant reading, as well application of the theoretical frameworks of reading to non-text media.

catDesc.name: religious studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of religion, theology, and religious studies.

catDesc.name: writing studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of rhetorics, digital rhetorics, and rhetoric and composition as a field.

catDesc.name: semantic web technologies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the semantic web, its associated practices, technologies, and standards. Includes articles about or implementing RDF (Resource Description Framework) and LOD (Linked Open Data). Sometimes called Web 3.0; not to be confused with Web3 or blockchain technology.

catDesc.name: social justice
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues of social justice and the study of social justice. This includes articles about social justice within and beyond digital humanities, as well as articles about implementing social justice practices in digital humanities projects.

catDesc.name: social media
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with social media.

catDesc.name: sound studies
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering sound and sound studies. This comprises all non-musical audio material (e.g. podcasts, radio, analysis of sound, and recordings of ambient soundscapes).

catDesc.name: information standards
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with the use and setting of shared standards across digital humanities projects and organizations.

catDesc.name: stylometry
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with tools and methods for stylistic analysis.

catDesc.name: tools
catDesc.gloss: Articles about digital tools of all kinds (from platforms to apps to workflows). This category also includes explicit critical frameworks, the presentation of new tools, tool reviews, and reports on tool adoption. Often closely linked with #project_report.

catDesc.name: transcription
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with transcription tools, methods, and workflows. This covers automated transcription, collaborative transcription and crowdsourced transcription.

catDesc.name: translations
catDesc.gloss: Articles covering the translation of texts (especially via translation tools) and reports on translation projects. This category does not cover coding languages.

catDesc.name: usability
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with users and user interfaces. This encompasses the experiences and needs of users as they interact with digital artifacts and tools of all kinds; it also covers discussions of user interfaces.

catDesc.name: art
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with visual art, e.g. sculpture, painting, and printmaking, the study of visual art, and digital tools dedicated to the study of art.

catDesc.name: web technologies
catDesc.gloss: Articles concerned with issues and technologies of the worldwide web and websites.

div.head: About the DHQ topical categories
div.p: DHQ has created a set of topic identifiers to help identify the subject areas of DHQ articles: both to assist readers in discovering articles on specific topics, and also to assist in identifying commonalities between articles. These identifiers do not attempt to provide a fine-grained mapping of all possible knowledge areas or anticipate all possible future subject areas for DHQ articles. They are more of a pragmatic attempt to map out the current subject domains within which DHQ articles are clustered.

The initial version is based on an analysis of several sources:
keywords used by the annual Digital Humanities Conference (both proposed by presenters and provided by the organizers)
keywords provided by DHQ article authors
the DHQ editors' own observation and analysis of the existing collection of DHQ articles Drawing on these materials, the DHQ editors assembled an initial list which was then reviewed for duplicates and synonyms, and then reviewed again to consolidate similar topics (such as "mobile applications" and "mobile design"). Because in many cases differences of terminology reflect discipline-specific usage, we have retained multiple descriptors for each topic area, grouped together under a single identifier.

div.head: Usage and expansion
div.p:
Each DHQ article contains in its metadata one or more identifiers which in turn reference items in this taxonomy. These topic areas will be used in several ways within the DHQ publishing system:
in the DHQ search interface, to enable readers to search for articles on a particular topic area
to generate a topic index that groups together articles by topic area
to support a "find similar" feature that generates for each article a list of other articles that share some or all of its topic areas

When an article is accepted for publication, its authors are prompted to choose appropriate topic identifiers from the DHQ list, and they may also propose new topical identifiers. Authors may also include one more more authorial keywords, which might be more specific (for instance, discipline-specific subject areas or terms). Authorially assigned keywords are immediately included in the article metadata. Proposed additional topic identifiers are reviewed by the DHQ editors at regular intervals and added to the formal list as appropriate. At intervals, the DHQ editors will also review authorially assigned keywords and determine whether additional identifiers are needed.
